article.intro: Let's practise colours around us. Read the English sentences with an adult if needed. Norsk støtte: Les og si ordene høyt.

sections.heading: Learn
sections.text: Colour words describe what we see. Use the words red, blue, green and yellow while pointing to real objects.

sections.heading: Example
sections.text: A red apple is red; the clear daytime sky can look blue.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.text: Say the key words aloud and make one new sentence of your own.

article.comprehension_check: Which English word names the colour of a red apple?
article.key_takeaway: Colour words describe what we see. Use the words red, blue, green and yellow while pointing to real objects.
article.worked_example: A red apple is red; the clear daytime sky can look blue.

practice.question: Which English word names the colour of a red apple?
practice.explanation: Colour words describe what we see. Use the words red, blue, green and yellow while pointing to real objects.

practice.question: Explain or demonstrate: colours around us. Use your own example.
practice.model_answer: A red apple is red; the clear daytime sky can look blue.

flashcards.front: Which English word names the colour of a red apple?
flashcards.back: Red

flashcards.front: What is important about colours around us?
flashcards.back: Colour words describe what we see. Use the words red, blue, green and yellow while pointing to real objects.

flashcards.front: Give an example.
flashcards.back: A red apple is red; the clear daytime sky can look blue.

article.intro: In this lesson you will practise present perfect through reading, speaking and writing.

sections.heading: Learn
sections.text: Present perfect connects a past event to the present in different ways. It uses have or has plus a past participle.

sections.heading: Example
sections.text: «I have visited London» is present perfect; «I visited London in 2023» is simple past.

sections.heading: Try it yourself
sections.text: Explain how the example works, then write an original sentence or paragraph that uses the same idea.

article.comprehension_check: Which sentence uses present perfect?
article.key_takeaway: Present perfect connects a past event to the present in different ways. It uses have or has plus a past participle.
article.worked_example: «I have visited London» is present perfect; «I visited London in 2023» is simple past.

practice.question: Which sentence uses present perfect?
practice.explanation: Present perfect connects a past event to the present in different ways. It uses have or has plus a past participle.

practice.question: Explain or demonstrate: present perfect. Use your own example.
practice.model_answer: «I have visited London» is present perfect; «I visited London in 2023» is simple past.

flashcards.front: Which sentence uses present perfect?
flashcards.back: I have visited London.

flashcards.front: What is important about present perfect?
flashcards.back: Present perfect connects a past event to the present in different ways. It uses have or has plus a past participle.

flashcards.front: Give an example.
flashcards.back: «I have visited London» is present perfect; «I visited London in 2023» is simple past.

article.intro: In this lesson you will practise literary themes and symbols through reading, speaking and writing.

sections.heading: Learn
sections.text: A story's theme is a central idea; a symbol may suggest something beyond its literal meaning. Interpretations need textual evidence.

sections.heading: Example
sections.text: A locked door may suggest exclusion if the story repeatedly connects it to being left out.

article.intro: In this lesson you will practise building an argument through reading, speaking and writing.

sections.heading: Example
